text.p: Exxon Corp said on Monday its Exxon Chemical Singapore and Esso Singapore subsidiaries are studying the feasibility of new facilities for the manufacture of ethylene, propylene, derivative products such as polyethylene and polypropylene, and lubricant basestocks.
The new plants would be built at the site of the Esso refinery on Pulau Ayer Chawan in Singapore, and would be integrated with the refinery, the company said..
Exxon said Esso Singapore is conducting the lubricant basestock feasibility study which is expected to be completed in about one year.
Exxon noted that it is the world's largest manufacturer of lubricant basestocks, which are the primary components used to produce motor oils and other lubricants.
The company said it is considering the use of hydrocracking/hydrodewaxing technologies to produce high quality basestocks and provide additional competitive feedstock to an ethylene plant.
The project would support marketing expansion for Esso branded lubricants and basestock sales to third parties, Exxon said.
It said Exxon Chemical Singapore signed a letter of intent for the chemical products feasibility study with the Singapore Economic Development Board earlier this year.
Exxon Chemical already operates two major specialty chemical plants at the Esso Singapore refinery site and is a partner in a joint venture aromatics complex nearing completion on the same site.

Ethylene is a basic chemical that is used in a number of processes to manufacture a wide range of products, including plastics. The ethylene plant would draw the majority of its feedstock from the Esso refinery in Singapore, Exxon said.
It said the plant also would be an efficient supplier of ethylene and propylene to Exxon Chemical and its customers in the Singapore area. -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.
